macro.story:
The tape is mixed. SPY closed at 741.30, up 0.42% on the day but flat over five days (-0.27%), sitting below its 50-day but comfortably above its 200-day (+6.6% above 200SMA). QQQ is weaker, down 0.92% over five days and down 3.05% over 21 days, with RSI at 40.8 and MACD bearish — a clear tech laggard. Under the hood, S&P 500 breadth is negative at 27.6% bullish vs 41.8% bearish, but 7 of 11 GICS sectors remain above their 50-day. VIX sits at 17.96, down 4.3% over five days — no fear spike. The 10Y yield is 4.67% (up 6.2% over 21 days), DXY firm at 101.45 in an uptrend, WTI has run +26% over 21 days to $88.83, and the 2s/10s spread is compressing (0.365, down 7% today). Engine C washout state is CALM — no timing signal engaged.

The tracked conversation attributes the split tape primarily to two forces. First, the dominant view leans firmly bullish on the AI infrastructure and compute build-out — Jensen Huang joining X to publish a letter on open models has become a rallying point, with sentiment framing open models as bullish for the AI buildout and pointing to a projected +253% surge in US data-center power demand as the multi-year driver. Second, a bearish cohort is flagging near-term risk: Intel erasing its +15% post-earnings pop and closing red, S&P 500 futures selling off intraday on Iran War escalation headlines, and the 30-day correlation between mega-cap AI capex spenders and semiconductors collapsing toward zero — a sign that the AI trade is bifurcating rather than moving as one bloc. This sentiment picture is broadly consistent with the price data: the strong AI-narrative bid has not prevented QQQ from underperforming, because the semis/software leg is weakening while hyperscalers hold up. There is also a separate, distinctly bullish thread noting record US equity ETF inflows (~$880B year-to-date, running at 2x pace), which helps explain why SPY stays above its 200-day despite the internal deterioration.

Sector data tells the rotation story cleanly. Energy is HOT (score 10.0, RSI 69.3), Real Estate HOT (9.2), Materials HOT with a fresh MACD bullish crossover (9.0), and Utilities HOT (8.2) — a classic defensive-plus-commodity mix leading. Financials, Healthcare, Industrials all qualify BULLISH but with bearish MACD — leadership without momentum confirmation yet. On the losing side: Technology (score 2.8, RSI 45.4, below 50SMA), Communication Services (score 1.5, RSI 37.7, below both 50 and 200SMA), Consumer Discretionary (score 1.0, RSI 32.4) — the growth-cyclical complex is bleeding. This is where oil's 26% 21-day rip lines up: refining margins are the specific Early-Runway signal today.

Forward watch: does QQQ hold its 685 support (RSI 40.8 is close to washout zone but not there, and SPY 200SMA is not tagged), or does the tech leg break and drag SPY through 739? If oil consolidates while energy names extend, refining continuation stays intact. If DXY breaks above 102 with 10Y through 4.70%, gold/silver headwinds intensify further. Watch VIX3M/VIX contango at 1.12 — still calm but has been slipping.

Energy equities (XLE, E&P names) face near-term margin compression from lower realized prices, but the broader equity market benefits. Transports and consumer discretionary are direct fuel-cost beneficiaries.

The regime reads CHOPPY/TRANSITIONAL (confidence 6/10) and SPY sits -0.8% below its 50SMA with breadth split roughly even (29% bullish vs 31.5% bearish across 479 names). This is not a trend-day tape; it is a rotation tape with one crowded winner and a lot of stalled middle.

**[CROSS-ASSET LENS]** The macro backdrop is actively unfriendly to the reflation side. The DXY_METALS_TAG signal is ACTIVE — DXY at 101.45 is above both its 21d and 50d SMAs, and that inverse to Gold/Silver/Copper HOLDS in backtest (corr -0.45, sustained in 70% of rolling 24-month windows). VIX at 18 with a normal contango term structure says stress is contained; the SPY RSI at 44.5 is trend posture, not a fade setup.

**[SECTOR & ROTATION LENS]** Money is flowing hard into Energy (XLE +11.6% 21d, +5.8% over 50SMA) — that leadership is real and tied to WTI +27% over 21d. Health Care (XLV +6.1%) and Financials (XLF +4.6%) are the quiet secondary bid. That is exits-not-entries territory; XLK-style chasing here has historically had near-zero median remaining gain.
